alt: Jesus commands an unclean spirit to depart as astonished onlookers watch in a synagogue.
caption: An imaginative depiction of Christ's authority in Mark 1:21-28. The visible spirit and architecture are artistic interpretations.

alt: An armoured believer holding a shield stands beside an open book, looking towards Christ in golden light.
caption: An allegory of the armour of God in Ephesians 6:10-18, not a literal battle or a complete depiction of every item of armour.

alt: Christ enthroned in light with angelic figures descending into dark clouds.
caption: Symbolic interpretation of divine judgement over rebellious angels. Scripture does not establish their appearance or this precise scene.

alt: Ancient travellers observe towering human figures on a distant ridge above a valley.
caption: An imaginative rendering of the spies' report in Numbers 13:30-33; it does not establish the Nephilim's actual height or ancestry.

alt: Christ enthroned above shadowed crowns, thrones and symbolic earthly and heavenly powers.
caption: An allegory of Christ's supremacy over powers, informed by Ephesians 1:20-23 and Colossians 1:15-17. The figures do not depict identified spiritual ranks.

alt: A shadowed accuser points towards a grieving man, with scenes evoking temptation in the background.
caption: A symbolic composite of accusation and temptation in Job, Genesis and the Gospels, not a literal single event or verified portrait of Satan.

alt: Jesus sits beside a restored man near a rocky lakeshore, with disciples and tombs behind them.
caption: An imaginative rendering of the restored man in Mark 5:15-20 and Luke 8:35-39. The setting, gesture and lighting are artistic interpretations.

alt: Jesus stands in a rocky desert as a shadowed figure gestures from a distant ridge beneath a glowing sky.
caption: An imaginative depiction of Christ's wilderness temptation in Matthew 4:1-11 and Luke 4:1-13. The tempter's appearance and the landscape are artistic interpretations.

alt: A robed figure on a ruined throne, with flies and figures pointing towards him.
caption: Symbolic interpretation drawing on Matthew 12:24-29 and 2 Kings 1:2-6. The throne, flies and figure's appearance are artistic choices; neither passage supplies a physical portrait.

alt: A winged figure rises above smoke and a swarm of locusts.
caption: Inspired by Revelation 9:1-11, which identifies the angel of the abyss as king over the locusts. His armour, wings, face and the rendered insects are artistic interpretations, not an exact portrayal of the vision.

alt: A shadowed figure sits in a rocky desert as a goat walks towards the wilderness.
caption: Combines the wilderness motif of Leviticus 16:8-22 with the personal figure in 1 Enoch 10:4-8. The juxtaposition is interpretative, not a claim that the two texts establish the same identity or that Leviticus describes a visible being.

alt: A robed figure amid ruined idols and broken tablets faces distant light surrounding Christ.
caption: An allegory of the opposition between Christ and Belial in 2 Corinthians 6:14-16. The personification and imagery are invented; the text does not establish a physical appearance.

alt: An armoured figure confronts luminous heavenly figures above Persian-inspired architecture.
caption: An imagined visualisation of the conflict in Daniel 10:13-21. The prince's armour, appearance, weapons and architectural setting are not described in that passage.

alt: A winged figure and a company of heavenly beings gather beside a mountain beneath a heavenly court.
caption: Inspired by the descent of the Watchers and their judgement in 1 Enoch 6 and 10, not a Biblical portrait. The wings, robes and composition are imaginative.

alt: An armoured figure with a spear stands above classical Greek-inspired architecture under storm clouds.
caption: A symbolic interpretation of the title in Daniel 10:20. The passage does not specify the figure's appearance or location. This image is not a portrait of a historical ruler or a judgement on Greek people.

alt: A luminous angelic figure gestures towards a shadowed figure recoiling from light beside people in prayer.
caption: An imagined composite of divine assistance and the demon's defeat in Tobit 3 and 8, a deuterocanonical text. The appearance and staging are artistic, not a literal reconstruction or practical instructions.

alt: A chained winged figure amid broken tablets faces a heavenly court.
caption: An allegorical depiction informed by the Enochic attribution in 1 Enoch 8:3 and the judgement of the Watchers in chapter 10. The appearance and objects are invented; the source does not describe this scene.

alt: A winged figure holds a celestial instrument beneath a darkened sky while other figures examine a book.
caption: Symbolic interpretation of the teaching attributed to Baraqijal in 1 Enoch 8:3. The figure, instruments and constellations are invented imagery, not a Biblical description or an instructional chart.

title: Saint Michael and the Dragon, from the Apocalypse
alt: Historical engraving depicting Saint Michael and angels in conflict with the dragon.
caption: A historical artistic interpretation of Revelation 12:7-9, rather than a contemporary account of heavenly conflict.

title: The Beast with Seven Heads and the Beast with Lamb's Horns, from The Apocalypse
credit: Gift of Mrs. Felix M. Warburg, 1940
alt: An intricate woodcut showing a seven-headed beast, a second horned beast and a heavenly scene above.
caption: Dürer's interpretation of the beasts of Revelation 13. The woodcut illustrates historical artistic reception of the vision rather than establishing the beasts' physical appearance.

title: The Fall of Man, from The Small Passion
alt: Renaissance woodcut of Adam and Eve in the garden with the serpent and tree.
caption: An artistic interpretation of Genesis 3 from Dürer's Small Passion series. It does not establish the serpent's appearance or the historical details of the garden.

title: The Last Judgment
alt: Hand-coloured medieval woodcut depicting the Last Judgement.
caption: A fifteenth-century Christian interpretation of final judgement, presented alongside the Biblical study rather than as a literal record of future events.

title: Saint Augustine of Hippo
artist: Pieter de Jode the younger, after Erasmus Quellinus II and Johannes Mantelius
alt: Seventeenth-century allegorical engraving of Augustine surrounded by figures and emblems.
caption: A later devotional and allegorical representation of Augustine, not a portrait taken from life or an illustration originally published with The City of God.

title: The Shade of the Prophet Samuel Invoked by King Saul and Conjured by the Witch of Endor
alt: Chalk drawing of Saul, the medium and the apparition of Samuel amid ominous clouds.
caption: Coypel's dramatic interpretation of 1 Samuel 28. The added imagery belongs to the artist, and the work does not settle the disputed nature of the apparition.

title: Saint Peter and Simon Magus
alt: Renaissance panel depicting Simon Magus falling in front of gathered witnesses.
caption: A later Christian tradition depicts Simon's fall before Nero. The event pictured is not recorded in Acts 8. The panel is included as evidence of historical artistic reception, not as an illustration of a Biblical event.

title: Satan Smiting Job with Boils
alt: Engraving depicting Satan afflicting Job, framed by Blake's decorative border.
caption: From Blake's Illustrations of the Book of Job, an artistic interpretation of Job 2:7. The figure's appearance and surrounding details are not descriptions supplied by Scripture.

title: The Transfiguration, after Raphael
medium: Brush and brown wash, white gouache over charcoal on blue paper
alt: Drawing after Raphael's Transfiguration composition, with Christ above the gathered figures below.
caption: The composition brings together the Transfiguration and the afflicted boy episode, which follow one another in Mark 9. It is a later artistic arrangement, not a clinical description or a record of supernatural appearance.

title: Christ in Limbo, from "The Small Woodcut Passion"
credit: The George Khuner Collection, Gift of Mrs. George Khuner, 1975
alt: Hand-coloured woodcut of Christ at the entrance to limbo.
caption: A historical representation of the descent of Christ, associated with the Christian tradition of the Harrowing of Hell. The work expresses one interpretation of Christ's victory; details of the depicted event are not explicitly narrated in Scripture.

title: The Fall of Satan
alt: Blake's engraved interpretation of the fall of Satan in his Book of Job series.
caption: This engraving belongs to Blake's Illustrations of the Book of Job, not an illustrated edition of Isaiah. It is included as a historical comparison with interpretations of Satan's fall, not evidence that Isaiah 14 directly names Satan.

title: Leaf from a Beatus Manuscript: the Fourth Angel Sounds the Trumpet and an Eagle Cries Woe
medium: Tempera, gold, and ink on parchment
credit: Purchase, The Cloisters Collection, Rogers and Harris Brisbane Dick Funds, and Joseph Pulitzer Bequest, 1991
alt: Medieval illuminated manuscript leaf with the fourth angel and the eagle from Revelation.
caption: A Spanish Beatus manuscript leaf illustrating Revelation 8:12-13 through medieval Christian commentary and art. It is a historical witness to reception of the Apocalypse, not an original manuscript of Revelation.

title: Manuscript Leaf with the Last Judgment, from a Book of Hours
credit: Gift of Max Falk, in honor of William D. Wixom, 1998
alt: French medieval miniature of Christ presiding over the Last Judgement, with angels and the dead rising from graves.
caption: A devotional illumination from a French Book of Hours. Its composition interprets final judgement in a medieval devotional context.

title: Manuscript Leaf Cutting from a Choir Book with an Illuminated Initial B and the Archangel Michael
medium: Tempera, gold, silver, ink on parchment
alt: Illuminated initial B with an armoured Archangel Michael and metallic decoration.
caption: An Italian choir-book cutting representing medieval devotion to Michael. The depiction of armour reflects historical artistic convention, not a Biblical description.
